whyEn: Exam weight 2/3. This chapter turns 'just a wound' into a testable clinical decision tree: wound classification, dressing and bandage choice, the bleeding-control ladder that ends in the tourniquet, and three named high-stakes conditions — compartment syndrome, crush syndrome, and the five phases of blast injury — are all fair game on both the COPR written exam and the practical stations. Lock in the numbers: the time thresholds for compartment syndrome and crush syndrome, the amputated-part preservation rules, and the five blast-injury phases.
whyZh: 考试权重 2/3。这一章把「不就是个伤口」变成一整套能考的临床决策树：伤口分类、敷料绷带的选择、从直接压迫一路走到止血带的止血阶梯，再加三个高分值的命名情况——筋膜间室综合征、挤压综合征、爆炸伤五阶段机制——笔试和实操站都会考。要死记的数字：筋膜间室综合征和挤压综合征各自的时间阈值、离断肢体保存规则、爆炸伤的五个阶段。

sections.titleZh: 引言、流行病学与皮肤结构

points.en: The skin is the body's largest organ and its interface with the outside world — soft-tissue injuries are common and often look dramatic, but the astute paramedic treats them as rarely the top priority in serious trauma; airway, breathing, and circulation still come first.
points.zh: 皮肤是人体最大的器官，也是身体与外界的接口——软组织损伤很常见，看着也吓人，但老练的急救员清楚它在严重创伤里很少是第一优先级；气道、呼吸、循环永远排在前面。

points.en: Soft tissue covers fat, muscle, tendon, ligament, synovial membrane, blood/lymph vessels, and nerve. Four injury mechanisms: blunt (energy exceeds tissue tolerance, e.g. falls/MVC), penetrating (an object breaches the skin), barotrauma (sudden pressure change, e.g. diving), and burns (thermal/chemical/electrical/other energy).
points.zh: 软组织涵盖脂肪、肌肉、肌腱、韧带、滑膜、血管淋巴管和神经。四种致伤机制：钝力（能量超出组织耐受，如跌落/车祸）、穿透（物体突破皮肤）、气压伤（突然的压力变化，如潜水）、烧伤（热/化学/电/其他能量）。

points.en: Soft-tissue trauma is the single leading form of injury overall and wound care is among the most common ED procedures, yet death from soft-tissue injury itself is uncommon — when it happens, it is almost always via hemorrhage or infection, so prevention (gloves, machine guarding, helmets, hi-vis clothing, teaching kids to avoid sharp objects) beats treatment.
points.zh: 软组织创伤是最常见的损伤类型，伤口护理也是急诊科最常做的操作之一，但单纯软组织损伤致死并不常见——一旦发生，几乎都是经由出血或感染，所以预防（手套、机械防护、头盔、高可见度服装、教孩子远离尖锐物）比事后治疗更划算。

points.en: Skin has two layers. Epidermis (outer, first-line barrier) has five sublayers; the outermost stratum corneum is nonliving and continuously shed (desquamation); melanocytes in the deeper layers produce melanin, which likely protects against UV.
points.zh: 皮肤分两层。表皮（外层，第一道屏障）共五层：最外的角质层是无活性细胞，通过脱屑不断更新；较深层的黑素细胞产生黑色素，可能起到防紫外线的作用。

points.en: Dermis is tough connective tissue built from collagen (tensile strength), elastin (elasticity/spring-back), and ground substance (compression resistance) — all made by fibroblasts. Papillary dermis feeds the epidermis and aids thermoregulation; reticular dermis provides strength.
points.zh: 真皮是坚韧的结缔组织，由胶原蛋白（抗拉强度）、弹力蛋白（弹性回弹）和基质（抗压性）构成，均由成纤维细胞合成。乳头层为表皮供给营养并参与体温调节；网状层提供强度。

points.en: Dermis houses immune cells (macrophages, lymphocytes, mast cells) plus nerve endings (touch/temp/pressure/pain), thermoregulating blood vessels, sweat glands (normal loss 500-1,000 mL/24h, up to 1,000 mL/hour with strenuous exercise), hair follicles (arrector pili → piloerection/gooseflesh; scalp hair lives 2-5 years and grows 1.5-3.9 mm/week), and sebaceous glands.
points.zh: 真皮内还有免疫细胞（巨噬细胞、淋巴细胞、肥大细胞）、感受触觉/温度/压力/疼痛的神经末梢、参与体温调节的血管、汗腺（正常 24 小时排汗 500-1,000 mL，剧烈运动时每小时可达 1,000 mL）、毛囊（立毛肌收缩→起鸡皮疙瘩；头皮毛发存活 2-5 年、每周长 1.5-3.9 mm）以及皮脂腺。

points.en: Subcutaneous tissue (superficial fascia) is mostly fat — insulation, cushioning, energy reserve. Deep fascia beneath it is dense fibrous tissue that sheaths and protects muscle and other structures.
points.zh: 皮下组织（浅筋膜）主要是脂肪——保温、缓冲、能量储备。其下的深筋膜是致密纤维组织，包裹并保护肌肉等结构。

points.en: Skin tension lines matter clinically: lacerations parallel to tension lines (static tension areas like the scalp) tend to stay closed with little help; those perpendicular gape open, heal slower, and scar worse. Dynamic-tension areas over moving muscle disrupt clotting with every movement, slowing healing further — this also matters when debriding or removing an impaled object.
points.zh: 皮肤张力线有临床意义：与张力线平行的裂伤（如头皮这类静态张力区）多能自行贴合；垂直的裂伤会张开、愈合更慢、疤痕更明显。位于活动肌肉上方的动态张力区，每次运动都会打断凝血过程，进一步拖慢愈合——清创或取出插入异物时也要考虑这一点。

sections.titleZh: 伤口愈合过程与愈合异常

points.en: A wound is any soft-tissue injury; healing is a series of overlapping stages aimed at restoring homeostasis — not necessarily the exact pre-injury state.
points.zh: 伤口指任何软组织损伤；愈合是一连串相互重叠的阶段，目标是恢复内环境稳态——不一定是恢复到伤前的原样。

points.en: Hemostasis: vessel injury triggers chemical release that constricts arteries/arterioles/some veins (capillaries lack smooth muscle, so they keep oozing slower); platelets aggregate into a plug, which a fibrin mesh from coagulation factors then strengthens.
points.zh: 止血期：血管损伤释放化学介质，使动脉、小动脉和部分静脉收缩（毛细血管没有平滑肌，所以仍会缓慢渗血）；血小板聚集形成血小板栓，再由凝血因子生成的纤维蛋白网加固。

points.en: Inflammation: granulocytes and macrophages arrive first as phagocytes and chemotactic signalers; histamine dilates nearby vessels (more blood/O2/immune cells in) and makes capillaries leaky (immune cells move in) — producing the five cardinal signs: rubor (redness), tumor (swelling), dolor (pain), calor (warmth), and functio laesa (loss of function).
points.zh: 炎症期：粒细胞和巨噬细胞最先抵达，负责吞噬和释放趋化信号；组胺使邻近血管扩张（带来更多血液/氧/免疫细胞）并让毛细血管通透性增加（免疫细胞得以迁入）——由此产生炎症五大体征：红（rubor）、肿（tumor）、痛（dolor）、热（calor）、功能丧失（functio laesa）。

points.en: Reconstruction trio: epithelialization (cells from the deepest of the five epidermal layers, the stratum germinativum, multiply across the wound edges — large/disrupted wounds rarely return to the pre-injury look), neovascularization (fragile new capillaries bud in over weeks to months, prone to minor bleeding), and collagen synthesis (fibroblast-made collagen stabilizes and joins wound edges but never restores original tissue strength).
points.zh: 重建三部曲：上皮化（细胞来自表皮五层中最深的生发层，向伤口边缘增殖迁移——大或破坏严重的伤口很难恢复到伤前外观）、新生血管化（脆弱的新生毛细血管数周至数月内长成，容易轻微出血）、胶原合成（成纤维细胞生成的胶原能稳定并拉合伤口边缘，但永远无法恢复组织原有的强度）。

points.en: Healing is slowed by high-motion body areas (fingers — splinting helps), medications (corticosteroids, NSAIDs, penicillin, colchicine, anticoagulants, immunosuppressants, antineoplastics), and conditions (advanced age, severe alcoholism, acute uremia, diabetes, hypoxia, severe anemia, peripheral vascular disease, malnutrition, advanced cancer, hepatic failure, cardiovascular disease).
points.zh: 以下因素会拖慢愈合：高活动部位（手指——夹板固定有帮助）、药物（糖皮质激素、非甾体抗炎药、青霉素、秋水仙碱、抗凝药、免疫抑制剂、抗肿瘤药）、以及基础疾病（高龄、重度酒精中毒、急性尿毒症、糖尿病、缺氧、重度贫血、外周血管病、营养不良、晚期癌症、肝衰竭、心血管疾病）。

points.en: High-infection-risk wounds: human/animal bites (warm moist mouth = bacterial haven; rabies risk from wild dogs, cats, bats, raccoons), an embedded foreign body/organic matter (leave it in place in the field unless it threatens the airway or chest compressions — it may be tamponading a lacerated vessel), injection wounds, wounds with significant devitalized tissue, and crush wounds.
points.zh: 高感染风险伤口：人/动物咬伤（口腔温暖潮湿是细菌温床；野狗、猫、蝙蝠、浣熊咬伤有狂犬病风险）、嵌入的异物或有机物（院前应留在原位，除非妨碍气道或胸外按压——它可能正压住一条撕裂的血管）、注射伤口、有大量失活组织的伤口、挤压伤伤口。

points.en: Abnormal scars: hypertrophic scar (excess collagen stays within the wound margins, favors high-tension areas like elbow/knee, more common with lighter pigmentation) vs keloid scar (grows beyond the wound margins and can outgrow the wound itself, favors ears/upper extremities/lower abdomen/sternum, more common with darker pigmentation).
points.zh: 异常瘢痕：增生性瘢痕（胶原过多但仍局限在伤口边界内，多见于肘、膝等高张力区，浅肤色人群更常见）vs 瘢痕疙瘩（长出伤口边界、可能比伤口本身还大，好发于耳、上肢、下腹部、胸骨，深肤色人群更常见）。

points.en: Wound closure: primary closure (edges brought together neatly), closure by secondary intent (dress a high-risk wound and let it heal on its own), and tertiary/delayed primary closure (irrigate and dress first, close 3-4 days later — for infection-prone wounds that would scar badly if closed early). Most open wounds should be closed within 6-8 hours; visible-area wounds (lips/face/eyebrows), gaping wounds, wounds over tension lines, degloving injuries, ring injuries, and skin tears are candidates for closure.
points.zh: 伤口闭合三种方式：一期闭合（整齐对合创缘）、二期愈合（给高风险伤口换药、让其自行愈合）、三期/延迟一期闭合（先冲洗换药、3-4 天后再闭合——用于感染风险高、早闭合会留难看疤痕的伤口）。多数开放伤应在 6-8 小时内闭合；显眼部位（唇/面/眉）、张开的伤口、位于张力线上的伤口、脱套伤、戒指伤、皮肤撕裂伤都是闭合的候选对象。

points.en: Infection signs: erythema, purulent discharge, warmth, edema, local discomfort; red streaking = lymphangitis; systemic signs (fever, rigors, chills, joint pain, hypotension) mean transport. Tetanus (Clostridium tetani, found in soil/manure/dust/GI tracts) produces a toxin causing bone-fracturing muscle contractions starting with lockjaw; mortality is about 30%; Canada boosts every 10 years, and an injured patient not immunized in the past 5-10 years should get an updated booster. Necrotizing fasciitis (usually polymicrobial, most often Streptococcus) is rare but carries 20-80% mortality, with pain out of proportion to exam findings as its hallmark, sometimes with central necrosis or subcutaneous emphysema from gas-forming bacteria — a surgical emergency needing early aggressive debridement, managed with contact-and-droplet precautions.
points.zh: 感染征象：红斑、脓性分泌物、发热、水肿、局部不适；红色条纹＝淋巴管炎；全身征象（发热、寒战、关节痛、低血压）需送医。破伤风（破伤风梭菌，存在于土壤/粪肥/灰尘/肠道）产生的毒素引发能致骨折的肌肉痉挛，常先表现为牙关紧闭；死亡率约 30%；加拿大每 10 年一次加强针，若病人过去 5-10 年内未接种、此次受伤应补种。坏死性筋膜炎（通常多菌种感染，最常见链球菌）罕见但死亡率高达 20-80%，标志性表现是疼痛程度与查体所见不成比例，有时伴中心坏死或产气菌导致的皮下气肿——属外科急症，需早期积极清创，处置时按接触加飞沫防护。

sections.titleZh: 闭合伤与开放伤的分类

points.en: Closed wound: no epidermal break. Contusion (bruise) — nerve trauma causes pain, fluid leak causes swelling; torn small dermal vessels produce ecchymosis (black-and-blue mark); torn large vessels produce a hematoma (a lump with bluish discolouration).
points.zh: 闭合伤：表皮未破。挫伤（瘀伤）——神经损伤致痛，液体渗出致肿；真皮小血管撕裂产生瘀斑（青紫色标记）；大血管撕裂则形成血肿（带青紫色的隆起肿块）。

points.en: Open wounds are more dangerous than closed ones for two reasons: contamination risk (microorganisms enter → infection) and greater blood-loss potential. A closed leg wound can lose up to about 2 L into the tissue before rising compartment pressure self-limits it; an open wound has no such ceiling and can cost the patient their entire blood volume.
points.zh: 开放伤比闭合伤更危险，原因有二：污染风险（微生物侵入→感染）和更大的失血潜力。闭合性小腿损伤最多能向组织内失血约 2 L，随后升高的间室压力会自行限制出血；开放伤没有这个上限，可以让病人流干全身的血量。

points.en: Conditions that always warrant ED transport even if the wound looks minor: compromise of nerves, vessels, muscles, tendons/ligaments; a foreign body or cosmetic complication; heavy contamination; wounds overlying joints; eye injuries; animal or human bites; puncture wounds.
points.zh: 以下情况即使伤口看着小也必须送医：神经、血管、肌肉、肌腱或韧带受累；存在异物或美容后遗顾虑；重度污染；伤口覆盖关节；眼部损伤；动物或人咬伤；穿刺伤。

points.en: Abrasion: superficial skin scraped off (road rash); oozes small amounts, often contaminated with dirt/debris, painful despite looking minor, and still an infection risk. Do not try to clean an abrasion in the field — just cover it lightly with a sterile dressing.
points.zh: 擦伤：皮肤表层被刮掉（如道路擦伤）；渗血量小，常混有泥土碎屑，看着轻但很痛，也有感染风险。院前不要尝试清洁擦伤——轻轻盖上无菌敷料即可。

points.en: Laceration: a cut from a sharp object, clean or jagged (a clean linear cut is often called an incision and heals better). Severity tracks depth and structures damaged; direct pressure to control bleeding is the first priority, and distal pulse/motor/sensory function must always be checked for deep lacerations.
points.zh: 裂伤：锐器造成的切口，可以整齐也可以参差不齐（整齐的线性切口常被称为切割伤，愈合更好）。严重程度取决于深度和受损结构；直接压迫止血是首要任务，深部裂伤必须检查远端脉搏/运动/感觉功能。

points.en: Puncture wound (nail, knife — technically a bullet wound too) often shows little external bleeding but can cause extensive, even fatal, internal bleeding and drives pathogens deep. Always suspect internal injury and shock. Special cases — an impaled object or an air-pressurized-device injury — call for immobilizing the affected part and any embedded object before transport.
points.zh: 穿刺伤（钉子、刀——严格说枪伤也算）外出血往往不多，却可能造成大量甚至致命的内出血，还会把病原体带入深部。要始终怀疑内伤和休克。特殊情形——插入异物或气压装置伤——需固定受伤部位和任何嵌入物后再转运。

points.en: Avulsion: a flap of skin torn loose, partial or complete; the main danger beyond bleeding and contamination is loss of blood supply if the pedicle is folded or kinked — the flap dies without prompt restoration of circulation, so gently irrigate with normal saline and unfold/reposition it.
points.zh: 撕脱伤：一片皮瓣被撕松，可部分或完全分离；除了出血和污染，最大的危险是蒂部被折叠或扭结后失去血供——若不尽快恢复循环，皮瓣会坏死，所以要用生理盐水轻柔冲洗后展开复位。

points.en: Amputation is an avulsion with complete loss of a body part. A sharp-object amputation often bleeds less than expected (vessels can still constrict); a crush or tearing amputation can exsanguinate rapidly without intervention. Wound edges are commonly jagged with sharp bone protrusion; a degloving injury is a specific amputation pattern where the skin unravels off the hand like a glove.
points.zh: 截肢是撕脱伤的极端形式——身体部位完全离断。锐器造成的截肢往往比预期出血少（血管仍能收缩）；挤压或撕扯造成的截肢若不干预可迅速大出血致命。断端多参差不齐并可能有锐利骨端外露；脱套伤是一种特殊的截肢模式，皮肤像脱手套一样从手上剥离。

points.en: Bleeding or edema inside a fascia-bound muscle compartment raises pressure and compromises circulation; it is most common in the extremities, can follow open or closed injury, and crush injuries carry a particularly high risk.
points.zh: 筋膜包裹的肌肉间室内出血或水肿会使压力升高、压迫循环；最常见于四肢，开放伤和闭合伤都可能引发，挤压伤的风险尤其高。

points.en: Classic teaching is the six Ps — Pain, Paraesthesia, Paresis, Pressure, Passive-stretch pain, Pulselessness — but skin temperature, colour, sensation, and pulse changes only appear once compartment pressure has already exceeded arterial pressure. That is a very LATE presentation.
points.zh: 经典教学是六个 P——疼痛（Pain）、感觉异常（Paraesthesia）、肌力减退（Paresis）、张力增高（Pressure）、被动牵拉痛（Passive stretch pain）、无脉（Pulselessness）——但皮温、肤色、感觉和脉搏的改变，要等到间室压力已经超过动脉压才会出现，这是非常晚期的表现。

points.en: Pain is usually the FIRST symptom: out of proportion to the exam and MOI, not relieved by analgesia, and worsened by passive stretch or active movement of the ischemic muscle (e.g., dorsiflexing the foot stretches the calf/superficial posterior compartment). A tense, swollen compartment on exam is another early clue.
points.zh: 疼痛通常是最早出现的症状：与查体和受伤机制不成比例、镇痛药缓解不了、被动牵拉或主动活动缺血肌肉时加重（例如把足背屈会牵拉小腿三头肌／浅后间室）。查体发现间室紧绷肿胀也是早期线索。

points.en: As pressure climbs inside the compartment, VENOUS return is compromised first, and arterial inflow only fails later — waiting for 'pulseless' as your trigger is dangerously late.
points.zh: 间室压力升高时，静脉回流最先被压闭，动脉血流后才受影响——如果把「摸不到脉」当作判断依据，已经晚了。

points.en: Compartment syndrome sustained beyond 6 hours carries a serious risk of irreversible local tissue death, requiring extensive, disfiguring surgical debridement and carrying a risk of sepsis.
points.zh: 筋膜间室综合征若持续超过 6 小时，局部组织出现不可逆坏死的风险明显升高，需要范围广、致残致丑的手术清创，还有脓毒症风险。

points.en: Definitive in-hospital treatment is fasciotomy (surgical incision of skin and fascia) — a limb-saving procedure that also prevents Volkmann contracture (a hand/finger/wrist deformity from forearm-muscle damage) and preserves sensation. Prehospital fasciotomy by medical direction is authorized only in very rare cases.
points.zh: 确定性院内治疗是筋膜切开术（切开皮肤和筋膜）——这是保肢手术，也能预防 Volkmann 挛缩（前臂肌肉损伤导致的手/指/腕畸形）并保留感觉。院前在医疗指导授权下做筋膜切开术极为罕见。

points.en: Compartment syndrome can complicate a fracture, open or closed, independent of a crush mechanism — suspect it any time there is a fracture plus pain disproportionate to what you'd expect.
points.zh: 无论是开放性还是闭合性骨折，都可能并发筋膜间室综合征，不一定要有挤压机制——只要骨折伴随的疼痛超出预期，就该怀疑它。

points.en: Scene safety always comes first — at a blast scene specifically, wait for police to declare it safe and screen for secondary devices before approaching; responders have died from secondary devices at intentional-explosion scenes.
points.zh: 现场安全永远排第一——尤其在爆炸现场，要等警方宣布安全并排查二次装置后才能靠近；曾有救援人员死于蓄意爆炸现场的二次装置。

points.en: Do not let a dramatic-looking soft-tissue wound hijack your initial assessment: general impression and threats-to-life come first, and a high-MOI patient with minor-looking external wounds still needs a high index of suspicion for internal damage.
points.zh: 不要让惨烈的软组织伤口打乱初步评估的节奏：先看总体印象和生命威胁；高能量机制的病人即便外伤看着轻，也要高度怀疑内部损伤。

points.en: Skin exam uses CTC — Colour, Temperature, Condition: pale/ashen means inadequate perfusion, cool and moist skin is an early shock sign. Note whether it is localized to the extremities or generalized.
points.zh: 皮肤检查用 CTC——颜色（Colour）、温度（Temperature）、状态（Condition）：苍白/灰白提示灌注不足，皮肤湿冷是休克的早期信号。要注意是局限于四肢还是全身性。

points.en: The rapid trauma assessment scan uses DCAP-BTLS — Deformities, Contusions, Abrasions, Punctures/Penetrations, Burns, Tenderness, Lacerations, Swelling — head-to-toe including the posterior surface; blood on your glove after examining hair-covered scalp counts as a positive finding even without a visible wound.
points.zh: 快速创伤评估用 DCAP-BTLS 逐项扫查——畸形、挫伤、擦伤、穿刺/穿透伤、烧伤、压痛、裂伤、肿胀——从头到脚，别忘了背面；摸过头发覆盖的头皮后手套上有血，即使看不到伤口也算阳性发现。

points.en: History must screen for bleeding-relevant medications: anticoagulants (warfarin, dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban) and antiplatelets (ASA, ticlopidine, ticagrelor, clopidogrel) turn small bleeds into big ones; also ask when the last tetanus booster was given.
points.zh: 问诊必须筛查影响出血的药物：抗凝药（华法林、达比加群、利伐沙班、阿哌沙班）和抗血小板药（阿司匹林、噻氯匹定、替格瑞洛、氯吡格雷）都能把小出血变成大出血；同时要问最近一次破伤风加强针是什么时候打的。

points.en: On-scene release/referral: minor isolated wounds with good distal PMS and a recent tetanus shot may be treated-and-released or referred per local protocol; for genital or other sensitive-area exams, a same-sex paramedic or a chaperone is preferred when feasible, without ever delaying actual care.
points.zh: 现场处置放行/转诊：轻微、孤立的伤口若远端脉搏/运动/感觉良好且近期打过破伤风针，可按当地方案就地处理放行或转诊；检查生殖器等敏感部位时，条件允许应尽量安排同性急救员或有人陪同，但绝不能因此耽误实际处置。

points.en: Reassessment cadence: stable patients every 15 minutes, more serious ones every 5 minutes; keep on-scene time under 10 minutes for significant-MOI patients and push detailed exams to the transport phase.
points.zh: 复评节奏：稳定病人每 15 分钟一次，病情较重的每 5 分钟一次；高能量机制的病人现场时间要控制在 10 分钟以内，详细体检留到转运途中做。

sections.titleEn: Bleeding Control: From Direct Pressure to Tourniquet
sections.titleZh: 出血控制：从直接压迫到止血带

points.en: PRICED covers significant CLOSED injuries: Protect (splint), Rest, Ice (with a towel barrier — never directly on skin), Compression (manual, then air splint), Elevate above the heart, and consider analgesic Drugs — pain is often undertreated, which itself prolongs recovery and risks chronic pain.
points.zh: PRICED 用于严重的闭合伤：保护（Protect，夹板固定）、休息（Rest）、冰敷（Ice，隔一层毛巾——绝不直接接触皮肤）、加压（Compression，先手压后用气夹板）、抬高（Elevate，高过心脏）、考虑镇痛药（Drugs）——疼痛常被低估，而低估会拖长恢复期、增加日后慢性痛的风险。

points.en: Two general principles govern ALL open wounds: control bleeding by the least invasive effective method, and keep the wound as clean as possible — irrigate copiously with sterile water/IV fluid/tap water, never pick out embedded debris in the field, and cover with a dry sterile dressing.
points.zh: 所有开放伤都遵循两条总原则：用最不侵入但有效的方法止血；尽量保持伤口清洁——用无菌水、静脉液或自来水大量冲洗，绝不在现场挑出嵌入的异物，最后盖上干燥无菌敷料。

points.en: Bleeding-colour vocabulary for handover: arterial is bright red and spurts with the pulse; venous is darker and flows steadily; capillary oozes slowly. If bleeding had already stopped before EMS arrived, use a familiar container as a reference — a pop can (355 mL) or a water bottle (500 mL) — to help the patient estimate volume lost.
points.zh: 交接时描述出血颜色：动脉血鲜红、随脉搏喷射；静脉血偏暗、持续流出；毛细血管渗血则是缓慢渗出。如果 EMS 到达前出血已止，可用熟悉的容器帮病人估算失血量——一罐汽水（355 mL）或一瓶水（500 mL）。

points.en: The textbook's five bleeding-control methods, least to most invasive: direct pressure → elevation → immobilization → hemostatic dressings → tourniquet. (BC's exam sequence differs — see bcAlerts.)
points.zh: 教材的五种止血方法，按侵入性从低到高：直接压迫→抬高→制动→止血敷料→止血带。（BC 考试顺序不同——见 bcAlerts。）

points.en: Direct pressure technique: sterile dressing plus firm gloved-hand pressure focused precisely on the bleeding point (not diffusely over the area), secured with a roller bandage; if bleeding continues, leave the original dressing and add a second on top; splint the extremity even without a suspected fracture, to cut movement and reinforce the dressing.
points.zh: 直接压迫技术：先盖无菌敷料，再用戴手套的手精准压在出血点（而不是笼统压一大片），用卷带固定；若持续出血，保留原敷料、在上面再加一层；即使不怀疑骨折也应夹板固定伤肢，以减少活动并加固敷料。

points.en: Elevation only slows venous bleeding and only works as an adjunct — never a stand-alone control method. Immobilization matters because motion (even of an uninjured limb) promotes blood flow, and motion of an injured limb disrupts clots and re-lacerates vessels.
points.zh: 抬高只能减缓静脉出血，且只能作为辅助手段——绝不能单独作为止血方法。制动之所以重要，是因为活动（哪怕是未受伤的肢体）会促进血流，受伤肢体的活动更会打断血凝块、再度撕裂血管。

points.en: Hemostatic dressings (Combat Gauze, QuikClot, HemCon, Celox): pack directly and tightly into the wound, hold direct pressure for 3 minutes, reassess, add more gauze if still bleeding, then cover with a bandage or pressure dressing. Never use on an open cranial wound; especially valuable where a tourniquet can't reach (axilla, groin).
points.zh: 止血敷料（Combat Gauze、QuikClot、HemCon、Celox）：直接紧密填入伤口，持续按压 3 分钟，复评，若仍出血再加一层纱布，最后包上绷带或加压敷料。绝不能用于开放性颅骨伤口；在止血带够不到的部位（腋窝、腹股沟）尤其有价值。

points.en: Tourniquet application: wide flat material only (never wire/rope/narrow bands), with padding over the artery, wrapped about 5-7 cm proximal to the wound, tightened with a windlass (stick/pencil) until bleeding stops AND the distal pulse disappears, secured and never covered — mark 'TK' and the exact application time somewhere visible; if bleeding persists, apply a second tourniquet proximal to the first.
points.zh: 止血带操作：只用宽而平的材料（绝不用铁丝、绳子等窄带），压迫点垫衬后绑在伤口近心端约 5-7 cm 处，用绞棒（木棍/铅笔）拧紧直到出血停止且远端脉搏消失，固定好且绝不遮盖——在显眼处标注「TK」和精确上带时间；若仍出血，在第一条近心端再加一条。

points.en: Tourniquet safety: a correctly applied one WILL hurt — that's not a sign it's wrong. Never loosen or remove it in the field once applied (risk of embolism release, rebleeding, or tourniquet shock); release is a hospital decision. A too-loose tourniquet can worsen bleeding by blocking venous return while arterial inflow continues.
points.zh: 止血带安全要点：正确上的止血带一定会痛——这不代表上错了。一旦上好，院前绝不松开或取下（有释放栓子、再出血或止血带休克的风险）；何时松开由医院决定。绑得太松反而会加重出血——因为挡住了静脉回流却挡不住动脉血流入。

points.en: Pain control: cold compress (through the dressing, not directly on skin) reduces pain and blood flow. If BLS measures fail, consider morphine ~0.05 mg/kg IV every 5 minutes (or fentanyl/acetaminophen/nitrous oxide/ketamine per protocol) — avoid NSAIDs (ketorolac, ibuprofen), which impair coagulation.
points.zh: 镇痛：隔着敷料冷敷（不要直接接触皮肤）可减轻疼痛和出血。若基础生命支持措施无效，可考虑吗啡约 0.05 mg/kg 静脉注射、每 5 分钟一次（或按协议使用芬太尼/对乙酰氨基酚/笑气/氯胺酮）——避免用非甾体抗炎药（酮咯酸、布洛芬），它们会影响凝血。

sections.titleEn: Special Wounds: Avulsions, Impaled Objects, and Amputated-Part Preservation
sections.titleZh: 特殊伤口处理：撕脱伤、插入异物与离断肢体保存

points.en: Avulsion management: irrigate a contaminated wound with normal saline or sterile water; for a partially avulsed flap, quickly irrigate then gently fold it back into anatomic alignment and hold it with a dry sterile compression dressing — never remove the flap regardless of size. Ice around (not on) the area can extend how long underlying muscle stays viable, but never let wound care delay transport of an unstable patient.
points.zh: 撕脱伤处理：污染的伤口用生理盐水或无菌水冲洗；部分撕脱的皮瓣先快速冲洗，再轻柔地把皮瓣折回原解剖位置，用干燥无菌加压敷料固定——不管皮瓣多大都不要去掉它。在周围（而非直接接触）冰敷可以延长深层肌肉存活的时间，但绝不能因处理伤口而拖延不稳定病人的转运。

points.en: Amputated-part preservation: rinse free of debris with cool sterile saline, wrap loosely in saline-moistened sterile gauze, seal in a plastic bag, then place in a cool protective container (e.g., a Styrofoam cooler) — keep it cold but never let it freeze.
points.zh: 离断肢体保存：先用冷无菌生理盐水冲净碎屑，用生理盐水湿润的无菌纱布松松包裹，装入塑料袋密封，再放进保冷容器（如泡沫箱）——保持低温但绝不能冻上。

points.en: Amputated-part never-do list: never warm it, never place it in water, never place it directly on ice (frostbite risk that can prevent reattachment), never use dry ice to cool it.
points.zh: 离断肢体绝对禁忌清单：绝不加温，绝不泡水，绝不直接放在冰上（会冻伤组织、断送再植可能），绝不用干冰降温。

points.en: Notify the receiving ED or medical control in advance for any limb amputation — they may redirect you to a reimplantation centre, and air transport can be considered if none is available locally.
points.zh: 任何肢体离断都要提前通知接收医院或医疗指导——他们可能会改道让你送去再植中心，若当地没有，可以考虑空中转运。

points.en: Impaled object rules: do NOT remove it in the field (risk of uncontrolled internal hemorrhage or further injury); control surrounding hemorrhage with direct pressure but never press directly on the object or the tissue immediately adjacent to it; do NOT shorten it unless it is genuinely too cumbersome to manage (e.g., a fence post through the chest) — any motion of the object can cause more damage.
points.zh: 插入异物处理原则：不要在现场拔出（可能引发不可控的内出血或进一步损伤）；用直接压迫控制周围出血，但绝不压在异物本身或其紧邻组织上；不要截短异物，除非它确实笨重到无法搬运（例如插入胸腔的篱笆桩）——任何晃动都可能造成更多损伤。

points.en: Stabilization technique: a bulky dressing plus splinting the limb (if applicable) to eliminate motion. For thin objects, stack gauze pads cut halfway through and overlap the cuts, then tape/bandage the stack; a triangular-bandage ring or a 'log house' of rolled gauze works for other shapes; larger objects can be secured with rolled towels or splinting material.
points.zh: 固定技巧：用厚敷料加夹板固定伤肢（如适用）以消除活动。较细的异物可用剪至一半深的纱布垫叠放、交错切口位置，再用胶带或绷带固定成一叠；也可用三角巾做成环，或用纱布卷搭成「井字架」；较大的异物可用卷起的毛巾或夹板材料固定。

points.en: An impaled object in the eye is a special case: never press on the eye itself (can express aqueous/vitreous humour). Stabilize by hand first, build the same cut-gauze stack, cap it with a paper or Styrofoam cup, and bandage it in place — cover BOTH eyes, because the uninjured eye's consensual movement can still injure the impaled one.
points.zh: 眼部插入异物是特例：绝不能压迫眼球本身（可能挤出房水或玻璃体）。先用手固定，再用同样的剪口纱布叠垫，顶端扣一个纸杯或泡沫杯，用绷带固定——要同时遮住双眼，因为健眼的联动运动仍会牵动伤眼。

points.en: Rare exceptions to 'never remove': medical direction may authorize removal if the object directly blocks the airway with a deteriorating patient, or interferes with chest compressions during a viable cardiac arrest, or the patient is impaled on something immovable — always coordinated through direct medical control.
points.zh: 「绝不拔除」的罕见例外：若异物直接阻塞气道且病情恶化、或妨碍心搏骤停病人的胸外按压、或病人被固定在无法移动的物体上，医疗指导可授权拔除——一律要联系在线医疗指导协调。

points.en: Scalp: bleeds out of proportion to wound size (rich blood supply); the rigid skull underneath makes direct pressure very effective — unless the skull itself is fractured, in which case press around (not directly on) the break, use a bulky dressing, and consider the temporal artery as a pressure point. Dressings tend to slide on the curved skull, and hair interferes with securing them.
points.zh: 头皮：出血量常与伤口大小不成比例（血供丰富）；下方坚硬的颅骨让直接压迫很有效——除非颅骨本身骨折，此时应压在骨折周围（而非骨折处本身），用厚敷料，并可以颞动脉作为压迫点。头皮呈弧形，敷料容易滑动，头发也会妨碍固定。

points.en: Face and neck: airway control always comes first if only one provider is available, since these injuries can threaten the airway directly. Jugular/carotid vessel injuries need direct pressure applied POSTERIORLY (away from the airway); with bilateral vessel involvement, compress only ONE side at a time. Open neck wounds need a FULLY occlusive dressing on all sides (unlike the chest) to block air being drawn into the circulation or trachea.
points.zh: 面部与颈部：若只有一名施救者，气道管理永远优先，因为这类损伤可能直接威胁气道。颈静脉/颈动脉损伤要向后方（远离气道方向）施加直接压迫；若双侧血管都受累，一次只能压一侧。开放性颈部伤口需要全周密闭的敷料（不同于胸部），以防空气被吸入循环或气管。

points.en: Thorax: assess by inspection, palpation, auscultation (at least two sites per side), and percussion — hyperresonance suggests pneumothorax, dullness suggests hemothorax. Open thoracic wounds get an occlusive dressing taped on THREE sides, creating a flutter valve that seals on inspiration and vents on expiration to keep a simple pneumothorax from progressing to a tension pneumothorax.
points.zh: 胸部：评估用视诊、触诊、听诊（每侧至少两处）和叩诊——过清音提示气胸，浊音提示血胸。开放性胸部伤口用封闭性敷料三边贴合，形成一个吸气时闭合、呼气时打开的活瓣，防止单纯气胸进展为张力性气胸。

points.en: Abdomen: visible ecchymosis suggests serious internal bleeding. Assume any high abdominal-wall wound communicates with the thoracic cavity and dress it the same three-sided occlusive way; blunt or penetrating trauma can lacerate solid organs (profuse bleeding) or rupture hollow organs (contents spill into the peritoneum) — either can be fatal, and a benign-looking wound rules out neither.
points.zh: 腹部：可见的瘀斑提示严重内出血。腹壁高位的伤口应假定与胸腔相通，同样用三边封闭敷料处理；钝性或穿透性创伤可能撕裂实质器官（大量出血）或破裂空腔器官（内容物溢入腹膜腔）——两者都可能致命，外观轻微不能排除任何一种。

points.en: Groin/hip and genital injuries are usually straightforward to dress with direct pressure, but manage with extra attention to modesty — a same-sex paramedic or chaperone is preferred when feasible, without delaying care; letting the patient self-apply the dressing can ease discomfort for everyone.
points.zh: 腹股沟/髋部和生殖器损伤通常用直接压迫加敷料就能处理，但要格外注意保护隐私——条件允许时优先安排同性急救员或有人陪同，但不能因此延误处置；让病人自行敷贴也能减少双方的尴尬。

points.en: Hand/wrist/finger: dress in the 'position of function' (a gauze roll placed in the palm) to preserve range of motion after prolonged immobilization; dress each finger separately so they don't stick together during healing. Elbow/knee wounds carry elevated neurovascular-injury risk (especially the elbow, with superficial vessels/nerves in a tight space) — always check distal neurovascular status.
points.zh: 手/腕/指：以「功能位」包扎（在手心放一卷纱布），保留长时间固定后的活动度；手指要分开包扎，避免愈合时粘连。肘部和膝部的伤口有较高的神经血管损伤风险（肘部尤其明显，因为血管神经浅表且空间狭窄）——务必检查远端神经血管状态。

points.en: A crush injury is a body part compressed between two solid objects, ranging from a trivial finger injury to life-threatening torso entrapment. Typical settings: structural collapse (earthquake, tornado, construction/industrial accidents, mudslide, MVC, warfare) or a limb pinned under an unconscious patient's own body weight; it can even be iatrogenic (an overly tight cast or compression device).
points.zh: 挤压伤指身体部位被夹在两个坚硬物体之间，轻则手指小伤，重则可危及生命的躯干嵌顿。常见场景：建筑倒塌、龙卷风、施工或工业事故、泥石流、车祸、战争，或无意识病人自身体重压住一侧肢体；也可能是医源性的（石膏或加压装置绑得过紧）。

points.en: External appearance can badly underestimate internal damage — a 'just swollen' limb may hide muscle destruction severe enough to cause systemic illness, especially past 4 hours of entrapment. Crushed vessels often lose the ability to constrict, so crush-injury bleeding is harder to control by standard methods than a clean wound.
points.zh: 外观可能严重低估内部损伤——「只是肿了」的肢体可能已藏着足以引发全身反应的肌肉毁损，被困超过 4 小时后尤其如此。被压碎的血管常失去收缩能力，所以挤压伤的出血比清爽伤口更难用常规方法控制。

points.en: Crush syndrome (rhabdomyolysis) mechanism: muscle trapped over 4 hours with compromised arterial flow undergoes necrosis, releasing potassium, purines, phosphate, lactic acid, myoglobin, thromboplastin, creatinine, and creatine kinase — but the compressing force traps these locally UNTIL the limb is freed, when they flood the systemic circulation.
points.zh: 挤压综合征（横纹肌溶解）机制：肌肉被困超过 4 小时、动脉血流受阻后发生坏死，释放钾、嘌呤、磷酸盐、乳酸、肌红蛋白、组织凝血活酶、肌酐和肌酸激酶——但压迫力会把这些物质困在局部，直到肢体获释才涌入全身循环。

points.en: 'Smiling death' is the classic crush-syndrome trap: the trapped patient is alert and talking with rescuers right up until the compressing object is removed, then suffers sudden cardiac arrest from the systemic hyperkalemia release and unmasked hypovolemia — which is why treatment should start BEFORE extrication whenever possible.
points.zh: 「微笑死亡」是挤压综合征的经典陷阱：被困病人在移除压迫物之前还神志清醒、能和救援人员交谈，压迫一解除，全身性高钾和被掩盖的低血容量就会立刻诱发心搏骤停——所以只要有条件，治疗应在解救之前就开始。

points.en: Crush injuries appear in up to 20% of survivors of major earthquakes (examples: Hyogo/Japan 1995, Marmara/Turkey 1999, Bam/Iran 2003, Haiti 2010, Christchurch/NZ 2011).
points.zh: 重大地震幸存者中，挤压伤的发生率可达 20%（例子：1995 年日本兵库、1999 年土耳其马尔马拉、2003 年伊朗巴姆、2010 年海地、2011 年新西兰克赖斯特彻奇）。

points.en: Scene safety comes first: building-collapse scenes need technical-rescue partnership, and intentional-explosion crush scenes carry the same secondary-device risk as any blast scene.
points.zh: 现场安全永远第一：建筑倒塌现场需要技术救援团队配合，蓄意爆炸导致的挤压伤现场同样有二次装置的风险。

points.en: Pre-extrication protocol: gain IV access BEFORE the crushing object is removed whenever possible (two large-bore lines; external jugular or, in an unconscious patient, an IO if extremities aren't accessible); run normal saline specifically — NOT lactated Ringer, because LR itself contains potassium. Renal-protective volume can be aggressive: as much as 8-24 L may be given in the first 24 hours in hospital to protect the kidneys from myoglobin/acid/phosphate damage and hypoperfusion-driven failure.
points.zh: 解救前处置：只要可能，应在移除压迫物之前建立静脉通路（两条大口径静脉，肢体无法穿刺时用颈外静脉，昏迷病人可用骨内通路）；输液选生理盐水——不用乳酸林格液，因为其本身含钾。保肾补液量可以很大：院内第一个 24 小时内液体量可高达 8-24 L，用以保护肾脏免受肌红蛋白、酸、磷酸盐损伤及低灌注导致的肾衰竭。

points.en: Hyperkalemia countermeasures (know for the exam): 10 units regular insulin IV plus 25-50 mL D50W (shifts K+ into cells), calcium (stabilizes the myocardium against arrhythmia), and high-dose inhaled salbutamol (also shifts K+ intracellularly); sodium bicarbonate alkalinizes blood/urine to protect the kidneys and correct metabolic acidosis; mannitol may serve as a diuretic — furosemide is avoided because it acidifies the urine.
points.zh: 高钾血症对策（考试要记）：10 单位普通胰岛素静脉注射加 25-50 mL 50% 葡萄糖（把钾推入细胞内）、钙剂（稳定心肌、防心律失常）、大剂量吸入沙丁胺醇（同样能把钾推入细胞）；碳酸氢钠使血液/尿液碱化，保护肾脏并纠正代谢性酸中毒；甘露醇可作利尿剂——不用呋塞米，因为它会使尿液酸化。

points.en: If pretreatment fluids/meds aren't possible before extrication, apply a tourniquet proximal to the crush site — it won't prevent crush syndrome outright, but it blunts reperfusion injury and buys time; weigh the limb risk against the systemic, potentially fatal, toxin release it prevents.
points.zh: 如果解救前来不及预处理补液和用药，可在挤压部位近心端上止血带——它不能完全阻止挤压综合征，但能减轻再灌注损伤、争取时间；要权衡肢体风险与阻止全身性、可能致命的毒素释放之间的取舍。

points.en: Post-extrication: rapid transport, vitals at least every 5 minutes, continuous ECG (watch for acidosis/hyperkalemia/hypotension dysrhythmias). On-scene amputation of a mangled limb is a rare, physician-level decision reserved for extrication emergencies given the high field-infection risk; consider a hyperbaric-capable destination, since early hyperbaric oxygen can reduce muscle necrosis and edema in crush syndrome.
points.zh: 解救之后：快速转运，生命体征至少每 5 分钟测一次，持续心电监护（警惕酸中毒/高钾/低血压引发的心律失常）。现场截肢是罕见且需医生级别决策，仅在解救紧急、且明知院前操作感染风险很高的情况下才考虑；可考虑送往有高压氧舱的医院，因为早期高压氧治疗能减少挤压综合征的肌肉坏死和水肿。

points.en: Five blast-injury mechanisms: primary, secondary, tertiary, quaternary, quinary — an exam-favourite classification to have cold.
points.zh: 爆炸伤有五种致伤机制：一级、二级、三级、四级、五级——这是考试爱考的分类，务必背熟。

points.en: Primary: the pressure wave itself, from air displacement and heat at the blast centre; hits air-filled cavities hardest (ears, lungs). Proximity to a bomb matters, but gas/dust explosions affect an entire area with no 'safe' zone; underwater blasts travel roughly 3x farther because water barely compresses; a confined space concentrates more force onto the body.
points.zh: 一级：压力波本身，源自爆炸中心的空气位移和高热；对含气腔隙（耳、肺）伤害最大。离炸弹越近越危险，但气体/粉尘类爆炸会波及整片区域、没有「安全区」；水下爆炸的影响范围约是空气中的 3 倍，因为水几乎不可压缩；密闭空间会让力量更集中地作用于身体。

points.en: Secondary: blunt/penetrating injury from flying debris and the (longer-lasting but less forceful) blast wind — bomb casing fragments, structural debris, nails, wood, and glass can all become high-speed impaling projectiles.
points.zh: 二级：飞散碎片造成的钝伤或穿透伤，以及持续时间更长但力量较弱的爆炸风——弹壳碎片、建筑残骸、钉子、木片、玻璃都可能变成高速插入体的抛射物。

points.en: Tertiary: the victim's own body is thrown against rigid surfaces (ground, walls, fixed objects) by the blast's displacement force. Quaternary: everything else the explosion directly causes — burns (flash to full-thickness), crush injuries from falling structural debris, and entrapment that can last days.
points.zh: 三级：爆炸的位移力把伤者本身抛掷、撞向坚硬表面（地面、墙壁、固定物体）。四级：爆炸直接引起的其他一切——烧伤（从闪光烧伤到全层烧伤）、坠落建筑残骸造成的挤压伤，以及可能持续数天的困陷。

points.en: Quinary: biologic, chemical, or radiologic contaminants deliberately added to the device (e.g., a 'dirty bomb'), dispersed by the blast for long-term harm — a specific terrorism concern.
points.zh: 五级：装置中蓄意加入的生物、化学或放射性污染物（如「脏弹」），随爆炸扩散造成长期伤害——这是恐怖主义相关的特殊关注点。

points.en: Field management priorities: treat as a mass-casualty, secondary-device-aware scene. Assess breath sounds frequently — the pressure wave itself can cause a pneumothorax that can progress to a lethal tension pneumothorax needing needle decompression; noncardiogenic pulmonary edema and pulmonary contusion with microhemorrhage can also develop and worsen ventilation over time even if initial symptoms look mild.
points.zh: 现场处置要点：按大量伤亡、有二次装置风险的现场对待。要频繁评估呼吸音——压力波本身就可能造成气胸，进而恶化为需要针刺减压的致命性张力性气胸；非心源性肺水肿和伴微出血的肺挫伤也可能逐渐发展，即使初期症状看似轻微，通气也会随时间恶化。

points.en: Abdominal injury from a blast (ruptured bowel, internal hemorrhage from the pressure wave bursting air-filled loops) is classically DELAYED in presentation — a benign-looking abdominal exam right after the blast does not rule it out. Use OPQRST for any abdominal pain and scan all quadrants for DCAP-BTLS.
points.zh: 爆炸导致的腹部损伤（肠管破裂、压力波撑破含气肠襻引起的内出血）典型表现是延迟出现——爆炸后立即查体腹部看似正常并不能排除它。任何腹痛都要用 OPQRST 问诊，并对四个象限做 DCAP-BTLS 扫查。

points.en: Ear injury is near-universal close to a blast: tympanic membrane rupture is common, hearing loss follows proximity, and vertigo (from inner-ear disruption) can trigger vomiting that threatens the airway. Secondary-phase projectiles get the same impaled-object rules as any other impalement, removed only if they block the airway and only per protocol/medical direction.
points.zh: 靠近爆炸中心的耳部损伤几乎必然发生：鼓膜破裂常见，听力损失与距离相关，内耳紊乱引起的眩晕可能诱发呕吐、威胁气道。二级爆炸伤造成的插入异物，处理原则与其他插入伤相同——只有在阻塞气道且符合协议或经医疗指导同意时才能拔除。

points.en: Document every contact fully: scene findings (e.g., vehicle damage, weapon calibre), patient ABCs, arrival presentation and body position, and every intervention given.
points.zh: 每次接触都要完整记录：现场发现（如车辆损毁程度、武器口径）、病人的气道呼吸循环情况、到达时的表现和体位、以及给予的每一项处置。

points.en: Describe wounds objectively and completely: size, location, depth, and associated complications, plus your distal neurovascular findings, range of motion, and any signs of infection.
points.zh: 客观完整地描述伤口：大小、位置、深度和相关并发症，加上远端神经血管检查结果、活动度，以及任何感染征象。

points.en: Capture demographics, medical history, medications, and allergies, along with the patient's response to each intervention (same/better/worse) and their understanding of it, and note which paramedic attended the patient during transport.
points.zh: 记录人口学信息、既往病史、用药和过敏史，以及病人对每项处置的反应（不变/好转/恶化）和理解程度，并注明转运途中由哪位急救员负责照护。

points.en: Gunshot-wound documentation carries extra legal weight — most shooting cases end up in court, so document the scene, injury, condition, and treatment with particular care, since you may be called to testify.
points.zh: 枪伤病例的记录有额外的法律分量——多数枪击案件最终会上法庭，所以对现场、伤情、病情和处置要格外仔细记录，因为你可能被传唤出庭作证。

atScene.en: Cold can be applied as early as the end of the primary survey, but only after you've checked and compared distal circulation between the injured and uninjured limb — don't withhold pain/swelling relief needlessly, and don't skip the circulation check either.
atScene.zh: 冷敷最早可以在初步评估结束时就用，但前提是先检查并对比伤肢和健肢的远端循环——不要没必要地拖延止痛消肿，也不要跳过循环检查这一步。

atScene.en: When a limb is pulseless distal to an injury, BC allows one careful realignment attempt toward the anatomical position: if the pulse returns, treat the patient as stable; if it stays pulseless, manage as unstable and load-and-go.
atScene.zh: 若伤口远端肢体摸不到脉搏，BC 允许小心地做一次复位尝试，把肢体调回解剖位置：脉搏恢复则按稳定处理；仍摸不到就按不稳定处理，立即装载转运。

atScene.en: When anchoring a patient's own account of blood loss, reach for something concrete — 'how many pop cans (355 mL) worth' beats 'a lot' every time.
atScene.zh: 让病人自述失血量时，找个具体的参照物——「相当于几罐汽水（355 mL）」远比「流了好多血」更有用。

atScene.en: A tourniquet that hurts is working correctly — don't let a conscious patient's complaints talk you into loosening or removing it; explain plainly that the pain is the price of saving the limb or the life.
atScene.zh: 止血带勒得痛才是正常现象——不要因为清醒病人喊痛就松开或取下，直接告诉他：这份痛是保住肢体或生命的代价。

atScene.en: With a multi-provider crew, bleeding control and airway management run in parallel, not in strict sequence — the paramedic at the head manages the airway while a partner works the hemorrhage.
atScene.zh: 多人team时，止血和管气道是同步进行的，不是严格先后顺序——头位的急救员管气道，搭档同时处理出血。

atScene.en: For any impaled object, 'leave it in place' has exactly two exceptions — it's blocking the airway, or it's blocking chest compressions in a viable arrest — and even then, reach for direct medical control first whenever you can.
atScene.zh: 任何插入异物，「留在原位」只有两个例外——阻塞气道，或妨碍可救心搏骤停病人的胸外按压——即便如此，条件允许也要先联系在线医疗指导。

atScene.en: Treat 'alert and chatting' as a warning sign, not reassurance, in any patient trapped under a crush force for hours — that is exactly the picture right before a crush-syndrome cardiac arrest on extrication.
atScene.zh: 被挤压困住数小时的病人若还神志清醒、能聊天，这不是安心的信号而是警报——挤压综合征在解救瞬间诱发心搏骤停之前，往往就是这个样子。

atScene.en: For genital or other sensitive-area wounds, a same-sex provider or chaperone is the goal — but never let modesty concerns delay actual bleeding control.
atScene.zh: 处理生殖器等敏感部位伤口，目标是安排同性施救者或有人陪同——但绝不能让顾及隐私拖延实际的止血处置。

confusions.en: 'Small entry wound = small injury' — wrong for punctures: a puncture wound routinely hides extensive, even fatal, internal damage behind an unremarkable-looking skin opening.
confusions.zh: 「入口小＝伤得轻」——穿刺伤最容易骗人：外表毫不起眼的小孔，里面可能藏着广泛甚至致命的内伤。

confusions.en: 'The bleeding stopped, so it's not serious' — for arterial bleeding, a falling BP can turn a dramatic spurt into a quiet ooze; keep reassessing instead of relaxing.
confusions.zh: 「不流血了＝没事了」——动脉出血在血压掉下来后，喷射会退化成静静地渗，该做的是持续复评而不是松一口气。

confusions.en: 'Compartment syndrome means a pulseless limb' — pulselessness is a LATE sign; by then, compartment pressure has already exceeded arterial pressure. The real early flag is pain out of proportion that analgesia doesn't touch.
confusions.zh: 「筋膜间室综合征＝摸不到脉」——无脉是晚期表现，此时间室压力早已超过动脉压。真正的早期信号是与查体不成比例、镇痛药压不住的疼痛。

confusions.en: 'Crush injuries mainly kill through the visible wound bleeding' — the deadlier threat is often the delayed, systemic hyperkalemia/rhabdomyolysis release AFTER the crushing force is removed ('smiling death'), not the wound itself.
confusions.zh: 「挤压伤主要靠伤口出血致命」——真正更致命的往往是解除压迫之后延迟出现的全身性高钾/横纹肌溶解释放（「微笑死亡」），而不是伤口本身。

confusions.en: Hypertrophic scar and keloid scar are not the same: hypertrophic stays within the wound margin (high-tension areas like elbow/knee, more common with lighter pigmentation); keloid grows beyond the margin and can outgrow the wound entirely (favors ears/arms/lower abdomen/sternum, more common with darker pigmentation).
confusions.zh: 增生性瘢痕和瘢痕疙瘩不是一回事：增生性瘢痕局限在伤口边界内（多见于肘膝等高张力区，浅肤色更常见）；瘢痕疙瘩长出边界、甚至比伤口本身还大（好发于耳/上肢/下腹/胸骨，深肤色更常见）。

confusions.en: 'An embedded foreign body should be pulled out so the wound can be cleaned properly' — wrong: it may be tamponading a lacerated vessel; leave it in place in the field unless it threatens the airway or chest compressions.
confusions.zh: 「嵌入的异物应该拔出来才能清创」——错：它可能正压住一条撕裂的血管，院前应留在原位，除非妨碍气道或胸外按压。

confusions.en: 'Ice controls bleeding, so put it straight on the skin' — always use a barrier (a damp towel) between ice and skin; direct contact can itself damage the tissue.
confusions.zh: 「冰能止血，所以直接敷在皮肤上」——冰和皮肤之间永远要隔一层（湿毛巾），直接接触本身就会损伤组织。

confusions.en: 'An air splint stops any bleeding' — it only reaches about 50 mmHg, so it helps with venous/capillary bleeding and swelling but cannot control an arterial bleed on its own; a tourniquet is the correct escalation.
confusions.zh: 「气夹板能止住任何出血」——它充气压力只有约 50 mmHg，能压住静脉/毛细血管出血和消肿，但压不住动脉出血；这时该升级用止血带。

mnemonics.name: PRICED
mnemonics.en: Closed-injury care: Protect, Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevate, consider analgesic Drugs.
mnemonics.zh: 闭合伤处理：保护(Protect)、休息(Rest)、冰敷(Ice)、加压(Compression)、抬高(Elevate)、考虑镇痛药(Drugs)。

mnemonics.name: RICES
mnemonics.en: Alternate mnemonic for the same idea: Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevate, Splint.
mnemonics.zh: 同一套思路的替代口诀：休息、冰敷、加压、抬高、夹板固定。

mnemonics.name: DCAP-BTLS
mnemonics.en: Rapid trauma scan: Deformities, Contusions, Abrasions, Punctures/penetrations, Burns, Tenderness, Lacerations, Swelling.
mnemonics.zh: 快速创伤扫查：畸形、挫伤、擦伤、穿刺/穿透伤、烧伤、压痛、裂伤、肿胀。

mnemonics.name: 六个 P，只有一个早
mnemonics.en: Compartment syndrome's six Ps — Pain, Paraesthesia, Paresis, Pressure, Passive-stretch pain, Pulselessness — but only Pain is early; the other five show up once you're already late.
mnemonics.zh: 筋膜间室综合征六个 P——疼痛、感觉异常、肌力减退、张力增高、被动牵拉痛、无脉——但只有「疼痛」是早期信号，其余五个出现时已经晚了。

mnemonics.name: 一二三四五级
mnemonics.en: Five blast phases in the order they strike: Primary (the wave) → Secondary (debris) → Tertiary (body thrown) → Quaternary (everything else, incl. burns/crush) → Quinary (added contaminants).
mnemonics.zh: 爆炸伤五阶段按打击顺序记：一级（压力波）→二级（碎片）→三级（人被抛出）→四级（其余一切，含烧伤/挤压）→五级（额外掺入的污染物）。

selfCheck.qEn: A patient's forearm has been trapped under rubble for 5 hours. He's alert and chatting with you. What must happen before the crew frees his arm, and why?
selfCheck.qZh: 病人前臂被压在瓦砾下已 5 小时，神志清楚、还在跟你说话。在队友解救他的手臂之前必须先做什么，为什么？
selfCheck.aEn: Get IV access (normal saline, not lactated Ringer) and be ready to manage hyperkalemia BEFORE extrication whenever possible — this is the 'smiling death' window; freeing the limb first can flood the circulation with potassium and myoglobin and trigger sudden cardiac arrest.
selfCheck.aZh: 只要条件允许，应在解救前建立静脉通路（生理盐水，不用乳酸林格液）并做好处理高钾血症的准备——这正是「微笑死亡」的窗口期；先解救会让钾和肌红蛋白涌入循环，诱发心搏骤停。

selfCheck.qEn: What is the single most reliable EARLY sign of compartment syndrome, and what's dangerously late about the six Ps?
selfCheck.qZh: 筋膜间室综合征最可靠的早期信号是什么？六个 P 里危险的「晚」体现在哪？
selfCheck.aEn: Pain out of proportion to the exam/MOI, unrelieved by analgesia and worse with passive stretch — that's early. The other five Ps (paraesthesia, paresis, pressure, and especially skin temperature/colour/sensation/pulse changes bundled under 'pulselessness') only appear once compartment pressure has already exceeded arterial pressure.
selfCheck.aZh: 与查体/机制不成比例、镇痛药压不住、被动牵拉时加重的疼痛——这是早期信号。其余五个 P（感觉异常、肌力减退、张力增高，尤其是归在「无脉」名下的皮温/肤色/感觉/脉搏改变）都要等到间室压力已经超过动脉压才出现。

selfCheck.qEn: List the four things you must NEVER do to a severed body part in the field, and the correct preservation steps.
selfCheck.qZh: 列出离断肢体在院前绝对不能做的四件事，以及正确的保存步骤。
selfCheck.aEn: Never warm it, place it in water, place it directly on ice, or use dry ice to cool it. Correct steps: rinse with cool sterile saline, wrap loosely in saline-moistened sterile gauze, seal in a plastic bag, and keep it cool (not frozen) in a protective container.
selfCheck.aZh: 绝不加温、绝不泡水、绝不直接放冰上、绝不用干冰降温。正确步骤：用冷无菌生理盐水冲净，湿润无菌纱布松松包裹，装入塑料袋密封，放进保冷容器保持低温（不冻结）。

selfCheck.qEn: Direct pressure fails on a bleeding forearm wound. Per BC guidelines, what's next, and how does the sequence change for a groin wound?
selfCheck.qZh: 前臂伤口直接压迫无效。按 BC 考纲下一步做什么？如果是腹股沟的伤口顺序又如何变化？
selfCheck.aEn: Forearm: after pressure dressing and positioning fail, apply a tourniquet proximal to the wound. Groin is a junctional area unsuited to a tourniquet, so pack the wound instead — but never pack a neck, chest, or abdominal wound.
selfCheck.aZh: 前臂：加压包扎和摆位都无效后，在伤口近心端上止血带。腹股沟是交界区、上不了止血带，改用伤口填塞——但颈部、胸部、腹部的伤口绝对不能填塞。

selfCheck.qEn: A stick is impaled in a patient's cheek. What are the two exceptions that would ever justify removing it in the field?
selfCheck.qZh: 一根木棍插入病人面颊。哪两种情况才能例外地在现场拔除它？
selfCheck.aEn: It is directly obstructing the airway with a rapidly deteriorating patient, or it is blocking chest compressions during a viable cardiac arrest — and even then, involve direct medical control whenever possible.
selfCheck.aZh: 异物直接阻塞气道且病情迅速恶化，或妨碍可救心搏骤停病人的胸外按压——即便如此，条件允许也要联系在线医疗指导。

bcAlerts.topicZh: 止血方法顺序与伤口填塞
bcAlerts.bookEn: Describes five methods from least to most invasive — direct pressure, elevation, immobilization, hemostatic dressings, tourniquet — and never names 'wound packing' as its own distinct technique.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材给出五种方法，从最不侵入到最侵入：直接压迫、抬高、制动、止血敷料、止血带——从未把「伤口填塞」列为独立技术。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's preferred order is direct pressure → pressure dressing → position the part (elevation) → position the patient → tourniquet → extremity wound packing (only when bleeding is still uncontrolled and the site isn't amenable to a tourniquet, i.e. junctional). Wound packing is explicitly banned on the neck, chest, or abdomen. (Full tourniquet-position detail is in Chapter 21's bcAlerts.)
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 的优先顺序是：直接压迫→加压包扎→摆放伤肢（抬高）→摆放病人→止血带→肢体伤口填塞（仅当仍止不住血、且部位不适合止血带即交界区时才用）。伤口填塞明确禁止用于颈部、胸部、腹部。（止血带顺位的完整细节见第 21 章 bcAlerts。）

bcAlerts.topicEn: Pulseless-limb realignment and the stable/unstable call
bcAlerts.topicZh: 远端无脉肢体的复位判定
bcAlerts.bookEn: This chapter does not describe a specific realignment protocol tied to a stable/unstable classification for a limb that is pulseless distal to an injury.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材本章没有针对「伤口远端无脉」给出复位操作和稳定/不稳定判定的具体规程。
bcAlerts.bcEn: One gentle realignment attempt toward the anatomical position is permitted when a limb is pulseless distal to an injury. If the pulse returns, treat the patient as stable; if it stays pulseless, manage as an unstable patient (load-and-go).
bcAlerts.bcZh: 当伤口远端肢体无脉时，允许做一次轻柔的复位尝试、把肢体调回解剖位置。若脉搏恢复，按稳定病人处理；若仍无脉，按不稳定病人处理（立即装载转运）。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Guidelines p.19 Wound Care, footnote 2

bcAlerts.bookEn: PRICED simply says 'apply ice' without a specific timing caveat.
bcAlerts.bookZh: PRICED 口诀只写「冰敷」，没有具体的时机限制说明。
bcAlerts.bcEn: Cold can be applied as early as the end of the primary survey — but only if distal circulation has been checked AND compared against the uninjured limb first.
bcAlerts.bcZh: 冷敷最早可以在初步评估结束时就用——但前提是先检查过远端循环，并且和健肢做过对比。
bcAlerts.ref: BC Guidelines p.19 Wound Care, footnote 3
